Neha / Grace / Priyom — looked through the draft SLA and ran the quick perf model against Sable's expected traffic patterns (Grace, please confirm if QPS below is accurate). Short answer: meeting 99.95% + P95 <100ms for uncontrolled shared capacity is high risk without dedicated capacity or strict traffic shaping. Notes: 

- Baseline on shared pools: typical P95 for their model (2k tokens avg, standard open model) oscillates between 90-140ms depending on queueing. Under burst scenarios P95 can spike >200ms.
- To reliably hold P95 <100ms we need either a reserved GPU pool sized for their peak 95th percentile or guaranteed burst tokens via a throttled ingress.
- Availability: 99.95% requires multi-zone redundancy plus on-call escalation and an SLA playbook (we already have this, but it needs to be appended to the contract).

Proposal (operational):
1) Pilot phase (8 weeks): commit to 99.9% uptime and P95 <120ms. Condition: provision a small Dedicated pool (single-region, multi-AZ) sized to Sable's 95th-percentile peak. Technical deliverables: routing rule pinned to dedicated pool, prefix/KV cache warmup, and extra monitoring hooks (token-level traces for their routes).
2) Post-pilot (production): move to 99.95% + P95 <100ms after capacity uplift to a full reserved cluster and a 4-week stabilization window.

Commercial asks: Dedicated pool implies a baseline monthly commit. Ballpark operational uplift is +30% on their monthly commitment for the dedicated capacity and a 90-day minimum. Priyom, please refine the cost and the provisioning ETA (I expect ~3-4 weeks to stand up the dedicated pool once we have capacity slots).

Risks / caveats to include in SLA language:
- Force majeure / cloud infra incidents exclusion
- Maintenance windows with prior notice (we can limit these but not eliminate)
- Performance regressions tied to model updates — require change-control and rollback windows

I'll attach a capacity sketch and a checklist for the runbook. If we go this route, infra needs an expedited capacity reservation and we should pre-clear the legal deviations for the SLA carve-outs.

-Marcus

Hi Sally — thanks for the patience while we scoped this. Below is our recommended path that balances operational risk and their pilot timing.

What we can sign for the pilot (mid-July start):
- Pilot (8 weeks): 99.9% uptime, P95 <120ms.
- Conditions: Sable signs a short Dedicated pool commitment (90-day minimum) to provision reserved capacity, and accepts a 30% uplift on the committed monthly baseline to cover the reservation and priority routing.

What we will commit to after pilot stabilization (targeted within 6–8 weeks post-pilot):
- Production: 99.95% uptime, P95 <100ms following capacity uplift and a 4-week stabilization/verification period.

Operational asks from Sable (to include in final SLA):
- Provide prospective pilot traffic profile (qps, burst windows, request size) by 5/11.
- Agree to an exclusion clause for cloud-wide incidents and planned maintenance windows with 72h notice.

Next steps / timeline:
1) If Sable agrees to the pilot terms above, sign the attached short-form SLA (DocuSign link): https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC123-sable-sla
2) Priyom to prepare a draft order form / pricing addendum reflecting the 90-day commit and +30% uplift (ETA: 2 business days).
3) Marcus will queue capacity provisioning upon signed order and expects ~3 weeks to have a dedicated pool ready.

Sally — if that sounds acceptable I can send the DocuSign and the HubSpot deal will be updated to reflect the special terms (link: https://hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-2027-042). Procurement, let me know if you need any additional language or evidence (we can share runbook excerpts and monitoring dashboards once the order is in).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the operational implications.
